subject: Re: Billing for long-running clinical assistant — windowing, rounding, and minimums
messages:
From: Aimee Park <aimee@heliohealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question for multi-turn clinical assistant

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One question came up from our engineering team about how we’d be billed for a single patient conversation that has lots of back-and-forth, a couple of tool calls (lookup patient record, scheduled-event call), and a 4,000-token context when you include system + history. In particular:

- Do you charge per HTTP request or per conversation/session?
- If a conversation is resumed within 18 hours, do we re-pay the full context length or only new tokens?
- Are there any minimums or rounding rules we should expect for small API calls (we have many short checks that are ~30 tokens each)?

We need concrete examples to model our cost projections for the pilot. Happy to hop on a quick call or you can send examples.

Best,
Aimee
Director of Product, HelioHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aimee Park <aimee@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question for multi-turn clinical assistant

Hi Aimee —

Great question — I put together a few concrete examples below that match common Helio patterns. High level first: Redwood bills per-token (input + output). We also apply a small per-call minimum and meter in fixed quanta for efficiency; however, for multi-turn conversations we have a rolling conversation window and prefix/KV caching that prevents recharging the whole transcript on every call.

Example 1 — Long turn with full context (one API request):
- Context sent: 4,000 tokens (system + history)
- Model response: 350 tokens
- Metering: charged for 4,350 tokens (input + output)
- Rounding/minimums: we round to the nearest 5-token quantum for per-request metering, so billed tokens = 4,350 rounded up to 4,350 (already divisible by 5).

Example 2 — Short check within same conversation (cached prefix):
- Conversation resumed within 18 hours; prefix (first 3,800 tokens) is served from KV cache and not re-sent to the model if you use the conversation_id route. We only send the recent delta (e.g., last user turn = 40 tokens) + response.
- Model request tokens: 40 input + 80 output = 120 tokens
- Billed tokens after rounding (5-token quantum) = 120 -> 120

Example 3 — Many tiny health-check calls (~30 tokens each):
- Each call still hits a per-call minimum of 25 tokens. We meter each call and round to the 5-token quantum, so a 30-token call is billed as 30 tokens (no extra rounding up). If you batch multiple checks in one request you get better amortization.

Notes on the rolling window and cache:
- Our default conversation window is a 24-hour rolling window. Calls that explicitly pass conversation_id and use the streaming/conversation route will benefit from KV prefix caching — you avoid re-transmitting the prefix tokens and only pay for the delta.
- If you reconstruct the whole history each time (i.e., you re-send the full transcript client-side), we will meter the full tokens you submit. So to get cost benefits use the conversation_id and incremental append APIs.

Discounts & minimums for pilots:
- For the pilot we can waive per-call minimums for the first 90 days (so tiny health-checks won't be rounded up), and provide a 15% usage credit against billed tokens in month 1 to help you validate cost models. Ben is cc'd and can confirm.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with worked examples for the Helio pilot and a draft SOW. Let me know if you want me to schedule 30 minutes this week to walk through the numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —
Thanks for the clear examples. Two quick internal clarifications before we lock the pilot concession: 

1) Minimum waiver: finance is good with waiving the 25-token per-call minimum for the 90-day pilot, but we need the SOW to explicitly say "pilot exempt from per-call minimums; normal metering applies after 90 days."
2) Usage credit: we can apply a one-time 15% credit in month 1 against billed token charges (post-metering rounding). Need legal to confirm on the SOW language for billing credits.

Karthik — can you sign off on the metering language below? Specifically: "conversation_id + KV caching prevents rebilling cached prefix tokens when the same conversation_id is used within a 24-hour rolling window; sending full history client-side will be billed for the full tokens transmitted."

If everyone agrees I'll route the SOW + credit note to legal and schedule for signature.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Agree with wording. A couple of precision points to avoid post-pilot disputes: 
- Change "24-hour rolling window" to "24-hour rolling KV-cache window from the last interaction for a given conversation_id" — that makes the boundary explicit.
- Add: "Metering quantum = 5 tokens; per-call minimum = 25 tokens (waived for pilot); rounding occurs after summing input+output tokens per request."

Marissa — please update the SOW with those two lines and I'll give legal the green light. Aimee — we'll send an updated SOW this afternoon and include the pilot credit schedule. Looking forward to the pilot.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Pricing & Packaging
